title: Focaccia
subtitle: Ligurian flatbread with olive oil, rosemary, and flaked salt
excerpt: A thick, pillowy flatbread drenched in olive oil, dimpled all over, scattered with rosemary and flaked sea salt, and baked until golden and crisp on the outside. The best bread to make for a dinner party.

recipe.sourceNotes: Focaccia (from the Latin focus, hearth) is the ancient flatbread of Liguria in northwest Italy, where the town of Recco and the city of Genoa are its heartland. It is one of the oldest breads in the European tradition, made since at least Roman times. The Ligurian focaccia is thick, soft, and drenched in olive oil both underneath and on top: the oil is the defining ingredient. The dimples (formed by pressing fingers into the dough) create pockets that hold the oil and seasoning. The standard toppings are rosemary and coarse salt; in Liguria, onion is also traditional. Focaccia is related to pizza but is thicker, more focussed on the bread itself than on toppings, and typically proofs twice before baking. The bread can serve as the base for sandwiches (the Ligurian focaccia di Recco version is a different, very thin cheese-filled bread).

recipeTools.notes: A deep baking tin, approximately 30 x 20 cm.

content.text: Use a generous amount of olive oil, more than feels comfortable. The oil pools in the dimples and around the base of the bread, producing the characteristic glossy, slightly crisp underside and soft, oily crumb that defines Ligurian focaccia. Use your best olive oil here: it is the primary flavour of the dish. After the second rise, press deep dimples with all your fingers before baking: the dimples should reach almost to the base of the tin.

items.preparation: or flaked sea salt, for the top

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, and fine salt. Add 350 ml of warm water and 3 tablespoons of olive oil. Mix to a sticky dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and stretchy. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave for 1 hour until doubled.

Pour 3 tablespoons of olive oil into a deep roasting tin. Tip the dough into the tin and stretch it gently to fill the corners. Drizzle over 2 more tablespoons of olive oil. Cover and leave for a further 45 minutes to 1 hour.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Press deep dimples all over the dough with your fingertips, reaching almost to the base. Scatter with rosemary and flaked salt. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil as soon as it comes out of the oven. Cool for 15 minutes before tearing.
